agents.heading: Runtime context for coding agents.
agents.body: Start with a ticket, diff, file or symbol. Your agent can read production history through MCP today. Automatic lookup for each change is in development.
agents.viewLabel: Explore what a coding agent can read

views.label: Paths
views.detail: Follow the route the application actually took.

views.label: Attempts
views.detail: See where work repeated within the same execution.

views.label: Outcomes
views.detail: Find the result the application reported at the end of each path.

coverage.heading: Runtime memory coverage
coverage.body: Planned coverage checks ask whether your agent has enough evidence to answer a runtime question. A tested observation is ready for traffic. An observed one has recorded real behavior.

items.question: Who maintains the observations?
items.answer: Repository agents can add observations in a normal pull request today. Planned adapters will reuse existing events and help agents repair gaps as the code changes. Your team sets collection policy and approves the merge.

items.question: What is Studio for?
items.answer: See what your coding agents know about runtime. Studio lets people inspect evidence and manage access. The planned setup also brings environments, integrations, policies and gaps into one place.

items.question: Can I inspect the source?
items.answer: Yes. You can run Flowmark locally. The SDK and core are open source under Apache 2.0, and the platform source is available under the Functional Source License.
